title: Resources goes live: the project's measured facts, no SOON chip
description:
SPIDR child 1 of task-e7a20a498ed0436380e5aca23cb81607 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). Dependency-free LEAF.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the Resources screen, built from reads that ALREADY EXIST, and the removal of its SOON freeze. Nothing else from the parent.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb - and the parent's cited line is WRONG, so do not plan against it. The parent says Resources is 'FROZEN with a SOON chip (apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/shell-model.ts:111)'. `grep -n SOON apps/control-room/src/v2/shell/shell-model.ts` returns NOTHING; :110-111 is just the nav entry's label and icon. THE ACTUAL MECHANISM: `shell-model.ts:25` declares `readonly live: boolean` per nav entry, and `nav-rail.tsx:112-124` renders the `SOON` StatusChip (testid `cr.nav.<id>.unavailable`) when the entry is unavailable. So unfreezing Resources means flipping its `live` flag and giving it a real screen - not deleting a chip.

THE FACTS ALL COME FROM EXISTING READS, so this row adds NO daemon route: repository (root, branch, HEAD) from the remote/activation reads; provider (CLI, credential SOURCE - never a value); store (path, size, last backup); policy revision from `/policy/read`; seat limit from `/sessions/read`. One fact per row, refusals rendered VERBATIM.

NOTE A NEIGHBOURING GAP, already filed: `/repository/remote/read` is SERVED by the daemon (http-listener-read-dispatch.ts:34 imports REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_PATH) but has NO browser decoder and is absent from dev-proxy-paths.ts - see comment-81312c74 on task-19d2329c. task-e6000b57fd374f78ba074b9f0f0f2c67 is planned to add that decoder. If this row needs the bound remote for its repository facts and that decoder has not landed, either consume what IS decoded today or coordinate - do not build a second decoder.
definitionOfDone: The Resources nav entry is LIVE: its `live` flag is true in shell-model.ts and the SOON chip no longer renders - assert the absence of testid `cr.nav.resources.unavailable`, which is the actual rendered marker, rather than grepping for the string SOON in a file that never contained it. The nav roster test is updated.

The screen renders the project's measured facts one per row from EXISTING reads - repository, provider (CLI and credential SOURCE, never a value), store (path, size, last backup), policy revision, seat limit - against a REAL daemon frame. A test asserts a named fact's value reaches the row.

NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS EVER RENDERED. Assert it: a frame whose provider section carries a credential-shaped value renders the SOURCE only, and a test greps the rendered output for the value and finds nothing. This is the one clause worth a hostile test, because a credential leaked into an operator screenshot cannot be recalled.

Every refusal renders VERBATIM with its code - a resources screen that silently omits a fact it could not read is indistinguishable from a project that has no such resource. Assert one refusing read renders its code and the others still render.
This row adds NO daemon route and NO new command kind: `git diff --stat` shows no file under apps/daemon/src. Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: BROWSER-ONLY. Every fact comes from a read the daemon already serves. If a fact has no read, render what IS available and say so in a step note - do not add a daemon route here (that is a different row's 8-touchpoint work).
NEVER RENDER A CREDENTIAL VALUE - only its source. This is the row's one hard safety property and it carries its own hostile test.
REAL FRAMES ONLY: fixtures come from a real daemon; the exact-key decoders reject hand-written ones.
ASCII-only sources (glyphs.ts) and apostrophe-free JSX text, or the scheduler package-boundary scan reds. Check any new testid namespace is free. Keep every production file under 250 lines.

implementationPlan.description: THE CREDENTIAL CLAUSE, with a hostile test — the one clause in this row that cannot be fixed after the fact. The provider row shows the credential SOURCE (a sign-in file, or an env var NAME) and NEVER a value. Assert it hostilely: build a frame whose provider section carries a credential-shaped value, render, and GREP THE RENDERED OUTPUT for that value — zero occurrences, while the source IS present. Note activation-read.ts:118 already documents this exact boundary (values are scrubbed because they reach "the operator's screen and into e2e screenshots") — follow that scrubbing rather than inventing a second one, and if a fact arrives unscrubbed from a read, that is a finding to record, not something to scrub locally and forget.
implementationPlan.note:
THE CREDENTIAL CLAUSE, with the hostile test. 10 tests in this file, all passing.

I DID NOT ADD A SECOND SCRUB, which the step forbids. The daemon owns the scrub at the boundary that publishes (activation-read.ts:113-131, `secretValues` + `scrub`, documented there as reaching "the operator's screen and into e2e screenshots"). What this row adds is a different thing: a CLOSED GRAMMAR over the one field the provider row reads. A scrub tries to recognise a secret and delete it, and fails open when it does not recognise one. A closed grammar recognises the SOURCE and renders nothing else, so it fails CLOSED. `resources-credential.ts` is that grammar, alone in its own module, 53 lines.

  /^credential\/([a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31})\/(env:[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}|login-file|ungated)$/u

matching exactly what the daemon writes at activation-receipts-measure.ts:89-104. An environment variable NAME is upper snake case and an API credential is not, so the grammar cannot match a value even when one is substituted for the name. Unmatched input yields null and the row states RESOURCES_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_UNRECOGNISED @ CONTROL_ROOM_RESOURCES where the source would have gone.

THE STRUCTURAL DECISION BEHIND IT: this screen renders NO free-form `reason` from ANY read, on any row. Refusals render code + layer (which DoD 4 wants verbatim) and a sentence this screen owns. `reason` is precisely the field the daemon's own comment names as the leak vector -- "a git stderr tail, an OS error string ... a host echoing its environment can carry a token into one" -- so the provider row not reading it is what makes the grep hold rather than a filter that has to be right every time.

THREE HOSTILE ARMS, each greps the rendered output for the value:
1. VALUE IN THE RECEIPT'S PROSE, ref well-formed. `reason: "fatal: env ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<value>"` (the exact measured leak activation-read.ts documents) and `hash: <value>`, arriving at the browser UNSCRUBBED. Zero occurrences in the rendered output, WHILE the source is present: provider.cli renders "claude" and provider.credential renders "the ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable". This is the arm that proves the pass is not "rendered nothing".
2. VALUE IN THE REF ITSELF: `ref: "credential/claude/env:<value>"`. Zero occurrences; BOTH provider rows carry RESOURCES_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_UNRECOGNISED and NO `cr.resources.value.provider.*` node exists. And `store.path` still renders -- failing closed on the provider blanks nothing else.
3. SIGN-IN FILE source with a value in the prose: renders "a signed-in credential file on this host", zero occurrences.

THE GREP IS OVER MORE THAN THE VISIBLE TEXT. `renderedText()` concatenates the screen's `textContent`, the screen's `innerHTML` and `document.body.innerHTML`, so a value hidden in an attribute, a title or a data-* attribute counts as an occurrence. Two assertions per arm: `not.toContain(value)` and `split(value).toHaveLength(1)`.

ANTI-VACUITY, because "the value is absent" is the easiest assertion in the world to satisfy by accident: `renderedText()` asserts the haystack is over 200 chars before returning it, so an arm cannot pass because nothing rendered, because the testid changed, or because the component threw. Arm 1 additionally asserts the positive (the source IS there).

THE GRAMMAR IS ASSERTED AGAINST THE PRODUCTION SURFACE, never a reimplementation: the three describes call the exported `credentialSource` / `credentialSourceWords` directly. The rejection sweep runs 10 shapes -- a value in the name position, a value in the whole source position, the bare value, `NAME=secret`, lowercase, a trailing segment, an embedded newline, a prefixed path, empty, null -- and asserts `rejected.length` is greater than 5 first, so a sweep that silently generated zero cases cannot pass.

NOTHING TO RECORD AS AN UNSCRUBBED-FACT FINDING. The step asked me to record it as a finding if a fact arrives unscrubbed from a real read rather than scrubbing locally. I cannot make that observation either way: there is no control-room daemon on this host to read from (both live ports answer `Upgrade Required` / http 426; measured in step 2). So this is stated as unobserved, not as clean. The unscrubbed frames above are DELIBERATE hostile inputs I constructed, not something a daemon handed me -- I am not reporting a real leak, and I have not hidden one.

The drill that proves these arms are not vacuous -- remove the scrubbing so the value reaches the render and watch the grep go RED -- is step 6(a), with the SHA256 restore proof the new untracked files require.

implementationPlan.note:
REFUSALS AND PARTIAL READS. 9 new arms in a new file; 19 tests across the resources directory, all passing.

EVERY ARM ASSERTS BOTH HALVES. Asserting only the refusal would pass on a screen that had blanked itself; asserting only the survivors would pass on one that hid the failure. So each arm names the refusing read's rows AND names, by id, the rows from other reads that must still carry a value. The `survivors()` helper asserts its id list is non-empty first, so an arm cannot pass by checking nothing.

  activation refuses  -> root, HEAD, provider CLI, provider credential, backup, distribution all carry ACTIVATION_READ_FORBIDDEN @ HTTP_LISTENER; remote, store path, policy revision, seat limit, seats in use all still render.
  policy refuses      -> the revision row alone; 6 other rows still render.
  sessions refuses    -> both seat rows alone; 4 others still render.

comments.content:
CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN DESCRIPTION (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05, before planning it). I wrote that the freeze mechanism is "a per-entry `live: boolean` declared at shell-model.ts:25". THAT IS WRONG, and it is the SECOND wrong line number this row has carried - the parent row said the SOON chip was at shell-model.ts:111, which was also false. Here is the measured mechanism, verified three ways:

1. `shell-model.ts:25` `readonly live: boolean` belongs to `ConnectionDescriptor` - the CONNECTED / LAGGING / DISCONNECTED / HISTORICAL state machine (:36-58). It has nothing to do with nav entries.
2. `nav-rail.tsx:80` is the real gate: `const unavailable = reason !== null;` - and :90 `disabled={unavailable}`, :118-121 renders the SOON `StatusChip` with testid `cr.nav.<id>.unavailable`.
3. The REASON comes from the destination: `shell-routes.ts:77-79` `readonly route: CordumRoute | null` and `readonly reason: NavUnavailableReason | null`, built at :100-101 -
     `? Object.freeze({ id, reason: "NAV_DESTINATION_NOT_BUILT" as const, route: null })`
     `: Object.freeze({ id, reason: null, route })`
   with stable reason codes at :60 and operator words at :68 (`NAV_UNAVAILABLE_LABELS[reason]`).

SO UNFREEZING RESOURCES MEANS: give it a real route in `shell-routes.ts` so the destination is built with `reason: null`, and ship the screen it routes to. It is NOT flipping a `live` flag, and it is NOT deleting a chip - the chip disappears on its own once `reason` is null. The file's own header (:12-15) states the design: "A destination the build cannot reach is DISABLED with the reason it is", which is why the chip must never be removed while the screen is missing.

ALSO MEASURED: there is no Resources directory under apps/control-room/src/v2/ today (the siblings are approvals, board, components, goals, live, ops, projects, runs, shell) - so the screen is genuinely new, not a stub to fill in.

THE FACTS THE SCREEN NEEDS ALREADY HAVE READS, so this row still adds no daemon route:
- `/activation/read` (http/activation-read.ts) carries `repository`, `store`, `distribution` and per-member receipt rows (`ActivationView` :69-83) - that is the repository and store half.
- `/health/read` (http/health-read.ts) carries `storePath` (:54, :85) and the provider pause view (:37-43), with `KNOWN_PROVIDERS` at :34.
- `/policy/read` carries the policy revision; `/sessions/read` carries the seat limit once task-92d84d38 lands.
Note activation-read.ts:118 already documents that values are scrubbed at the boundary because they reach "the operator's screen and into e2e screenshots" - that is the same concern as this row's credential clause, and the same boundary to follow.

DoD 1 IS AMENDED accordingly: assert the destination is built with `reason: null` and that testid `cr.nav.resources.unavailable` is absent. Do not grep shell-model.ts for a `live` flag that governs nothing here.

STEP 3 FINDING: AN UNNAMED CONSUMER OF THE FREEZE, plus the structural consequence of unfreezing the LAST unbuilt destination. Filed per global rail 20; disclosing rather than quietly absorbing.

1. THE UNNAMED CONSUMER. The plan named the nav roster test (cordum-app.test.tsx). It did NOT name apps/control-room/src/v2/styles/cordum-shell-responsive.test.tsx, which also pins the frozen rendering and went RED on the route change with two failures:

  AssertionError: expected 'Resources7' to contain 'not available yet'
  FAIL ... > targets the badge of an item that will not press, which keeps a visible title
  (at :126 `expect(approvals.hasAttribute("disabled")).toBe(true)`)

Neither arm is ABOUT Resources. Their subjects are (a) the SOON chip is what the NAV_BADGE selector selects and a non-pressing item still explains itself by a visible title, and (b) a daemon-supplied count stays inside a disabled button's own accessible name -- the arms that exist because `display:none` on the narrow rail once dropped a wired count out of the accessible name without trace. `resources` was merely the one destination this build had not shipped, so it was the convenient stand-in; the local variable is even still named `approvals`, from the copy it was made from. A symbol grep for `resources` would have found it; the plan's affectedFiles did not.

I did NOT rename or reformat the producer to evade the check (rail 20's prohibition). I injected an unbuilt roster through the shell's EXISTING `navDestinations` prop, so both arms keep testing exactly what they always tested. Same treatment, same reason, in cordum-app.test.tsx.

2. THE STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE, which is the more important half. `resources` was the LAST destination on the `NAV_DESTINATION_NOT_BUILT` branch. `resolveNavDestinations()` now reports SIX reachable and ZERO unavailable. Every existing arm that read the disabled/SOON behaviour as `resolveNavDestinations().filter((d) => d.reason !== null)` would now iterate ZERO entries and pass while asserting NOTHING -- a textbook vacuous green, and it would have hidden the whole chip mechanism silently rather than loudly. Three arms were in that position (two in cordum-shell-responsive.test.tsx, one in cordum-app.test.tsx's "keeps an unavailable destination disabled and naming its reason while a navigator is wired").

Only ONE of them said so out loud: the roster test carried `expect(unavailable.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`, which failed and pointed at the rest. That guard is the reason this was caught at all.

Every one now drives the arm from an injected all-unbuilt roster (`UNBUILT_ROSTER`), so the machinery stays covered on its own terms and does not depend on the accident of some destination remaining unshipped. The chip machinery, the reason codes and the `shell-routes.ts:12-15` design are untouched, exactly as step 3 required -- `resources` only moved from one branch of the construction to the other.

3. THE ROSTER TEST'S COUNTS ARE NOW SET EQUALITY, NOT NUMBERS. It previously read `expect(reachable).toHaveLength(5)` and `expect(unavailable).toHaveLength(NAV_IDS.length - 5)`. A hard-coded 5 with a derived complement re-encodes the same number twice and says nothing about WHICH destinations are reachable. It now asserts `reachable.map(d => d.id)` EQUALS `[...NAV_IDS]` and `unavailable` is empty, so a destination added to the rail without a route reds here instead of quietly shrinking a count that still matched some other arithmetic. `CORDUM_ROUTE_KINDS` went 6 -> 7 at cordum-app.test.tsx:613, the one hard-coded count consumer measured in step 1.
